items: The government raises gas cuts to fertiliser and methanol plants to 33% from 20% and notifies Ezz Steel of a 30% cut, with no end date → Asian LNG prices jump about 36% in a month, so Egypt saves gas for power and defers five of 15 November cargoes.
Abu Qir Fertilizers falls 5.78% and MOPCO 5.85% on Sunday as the EGX30 slips 0.67% to 50,812 → the gas cuts hit output at Egypt's largest urea exporters just as urea prices rise.
Evergreen's Ever Eon crosses the Suez Canal on Sunday, the line's first transit in nearly three years → the return of another major carrier supports canal revenue and dollar inflows.

Brent falls 1.5% to $96.91 in Asia on Monday as Trump says new strikes on Iran are very unlikely while talks progress → a US land blockade is now in effect, but de-escalation hopes outweigh new shipping attacks.

Egypt's annual headline inflation eases to 12% in October from 12.8% in September, with monthly inflation at 0.6% → slower inflation after the CBE's 100 bp hike widens the real rate and supports the case for holding rates.
Goldman Sachs says the pound is more than 30% undervalued and sees it at 50 per dollar in 12 months → a top bank's buy call can draw carry-trade money back into Egyptian debt.
The cabinet raises export rebates by an average of 35% and covers up to half of freight costs to new markets → the EGP 48 bn programme aims to lift exports and bring in more dollars.

The US sets up a task force to cut Iran's land supply routes as more blasts hit Qeshm and two tankers strike mines near Hormuz → the war widens even as Qatar-mediated talks continue, keeping oil and shipping risk high.

Cabinet orders three months of spending cuts: government electricity use down 20%, vehicle fuel down at least 30%, and no new projects or car purchases → the state is cutting its own fuel and dollar needs, a sign of fiscal strain but also of lower demand for FX.

The pound ends the week at EGP 54.01 per dollar at the CBE, with the dollar down about 2.12 pounds (3.78%) over the week → foreign money returns to Egyptian T-bills, and one banker sees 50 to 52 if inflows last.
Brent ends Friday at $98.32 as oil futures post their biggest weekly drop since 2022 → Gulf exports recover and traders bet on a faster end to the Iran war, which eases Egypt's import bill.
EGX30 ends the week at 51,152.73, up about 4.9% from Sunday's close (derived) after three straight gains → the pound's rally and falling oil bring buyers back; market cap reaches EGP 4.05 tn.

EGX30 rises 0.99% to 51,152.73 on Thursday, its third straight gain, with 169 stocks up and foreigners the only net buyers → a firmer pound and lower oil bring foreign money back; market cap reaches EGP 4.05 tn.

The pound strengthens to EGP 54.01 per dollar at the CBE on Thursday evening, after 54.77 on Wednesday → foreign investors turn net buyers of Egyptian T-bills ($112.3 mn on Wednesday) as oil falls, easing dollar demand.
Net international reserves reach a record $57.5 bn at end-October, up about $152 mn from September → a record buffer gives the CBE more room to support the pound as the IMF programme nears its end.

Brent rebounds 3.9% to $98.29 on Thursday after tanker attacks in Hormuz, a day after an 8.7% fall → Iran says Hormuz stays shut until its seven conditions are met, so oil swings remain a risk to Egypt's import bill.

Brent settles 8.7% lower at $94.62 on Wednesday, its first close under $100 since September, after Vance blames the midterm defeat on the Iran war → markets bet Washington wants out of the war; oil down more than 14% this week sharply cuts Egypt's fuel and LNG import bill.
The pound gains 65 piasters in one session to EGP 54.77 per dollar at the CBE → falling oil and the 100 bp hike ease dollar demand; a stronger pound lowers import costs and inflation pressure.

EGX30 jumps 2.83% to 50,650.18, back above 50,000, as 197 stocks rise and foreign institutions net buy EGP 338.7 mn → peace hopes, cheaper oil and a firmer pound pull foreign money back; pharma and consumer names lead.

Iran calls the US reply to its Hormuz plan unconvincing but Qatar says both sides stay committed, and Trump tells the FT he has no immediate plans to strike → talks continue despite attacks on shipping, keeping a deal and lower energy costs in play for Egypt.
The EBRD, the IFC and Helikon each disclose about 6.9% of Banque du Caire after buying EGP 16.7 bn of shares at EGP 5.30 → anchor foreign holders give the new listing a stable shareholder base.

stories.h: Urban inflation slows to a nine-month low of 12.7% in October
stories.what: Urban inflation falls to 12.7% in October from 13.9% in September, and monthly inflation slows to 0.7% from 1.3%. Core inflation eases to 13.1% from 14.1%, though its monthly rate rises to 1.2% from 0.8%. Food prices rise 1.1% on the month after 2.8% in September, while transport rises 1.4%. JPMorgan raises its December inflation forecast to 14.3% from 13.4%, and Deutsche Bank warns of high FX pass-through.
stories.why: Food price growth slows sharply; the base effect from last year still helps.
stories.aff: Real interest rates, household spending and the CBE's 17 December decision.
stories.eg: With the deposit rate at 20%, the real rate is about 7.3 points (derived), so the CBE has room to hold.
stories.egx: Bullish for banks and consumer names; the monthly core pickup is a caution.

stories.h: Brent drops 5.85% as Trump signals restraint on Iran
stories.what: Brent falls 5.85% on Monday and trades at $91.88 on Tuesday morning, down another 70 cents; WTI is at $86.07. Trump says he will hold off on new strikes after appeals from regional states, while the naval blockade stays. OPEC output rises in October, led by Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Iraq. Brent is about 22% below its 30 October high of $118. "The market continues to prioritise President Trump's more conciliatory tone," says KCM Trade's Tim Waterer.
stories.why: Traders bet the war is winding down, though Iran still attacks ships in Hormuz.
stories.aff: Egypt's fuel import bill, the pound and inflation.
stories.eg: Brent near $92 eases the cost of Egypt's fuel imports.
stories.egx: Bullish for importers and energy users; mildly bearish for oil-linked names.

key.l: ballistic missiles Saudi Arabia downs after a Houthi pipeline attack

stories.h: Trump calls the Iran war effectively over as Houthis hit a Saudi pipeline
stories.what: After meeting Qatar's prime minister, Trump says the war is effectively over militarily but keeps the blockade at the request of Iran's neighbours. Iran dismisses this and lists its terms: sanctions relief, frozen funds, a new Hormuz route agreed with Oman and an end to fighting on all fronts. Saudi Arabia downs two ballistic missiles and a cruise missile after a Houthi strike causes a limited fire on the East-West pipeline; Saudi officials say pipeline operations are unaffected.
stories.why: Washington signals a wind-down while Iran and its allies keep pressure on Gulf energy routes.
stories.aff: Gulf oil exports, Red Sea shipping and regional risk premiums.
stories.eg: A ceasefire would ease Egypt's energy costs and help the Suez recovery.
stories.egx: Neutral until a deal is signed.

stories.h: EGX30 rises 1.19% on local buying as foreigners sell EGP 303 mn
stories.src: Amwal Al Ghad; Arab Finance; EnterpriseAM
stories.what: The EGX30 rises 1.19% to 51,414.93 on Monday and the EGX70 1.54%; turnover is EGP 10.05 bn and market cap EGP 4.09 tn. Egyptians net buy EGP 347.8 mn while foreigners net sell EGP 302.9 mn. e-finance (+5.11%), Juhayna (+5.07%) and Telecom Egypt (+3.32%) lead the table. EnterpriseAM says retail investors made 74.9% of turnover in October and some borrowed at up to 50% to buy stocks.
stories.why: Lower oil and slower inflation lift sentiment; foreigners have net sold EGP 13.5 bn this year, EnterpriseAM says.
stories.aff: Blue chips, small caps and retail investors using margin.
stories.eg: The market relies on local retail money while foreign investors sell.
stories.egx: Bullish in the short term; margin debt is a risk in a sharper fall.
stories.names: e-finance, Juhayna, Telecom Egypt (up); Abu Qir Fertilizers, MOPCO (down).

key.l: Egypt Aluminum's Q1 net profit growth

stories.h: Egypt Aluminum's quarterly profit more than doubles to EGP 4.93 bn
stories.what: Egypt Aluminum's net profit rises 104% to EGP 4.928 bn in the quarter to end-September, from EGP 2.415 bn a year earlier. Net sales rise 6.35% to EGP 12.046 bn and earnings per share reach EGP 11.95 from EGP 5.86.
stories.why: Profit grows much faster than sales; the report does not explain the drivers.
stories.eg: A stronger Egypt Aluminum adds export earnings and value to a state-held company.
stories.egx: Bullish for Egypt Aluminum; the stock still falls 0.79% on Monday.

key.l: domestic borrowing in the first four months of FY2026/27

stories.h: Government weighs investing state entities' surpluses in its own debt
stories.what: Finance Minister Ahmed Kouchouk presents a study to President Sisi on putting part of state entities' surpluses into government securities, which he says would cut borrowing needs at home and abroad. The state borrows about EGP 4.3 tn at home in the first four months of FY2026/27, almost all to refinance, and T-bills make up 85% of accepted domestic issuance last quarter.
stories.why: Short maturities force constant refinancing at high rates.
stories.aff: T-bill supply, yields and bank interest income.
stories.eg: Less market borrowing could ease yields over time.
stories.egx: Neutral for banks now; mildly bearish for their bill income if supply shrinks.

key.l: gas cut Abu Qir confirms from 8 November

stories.h: Abu Qir Fertilizers confirms a 33% gas cut and shifts loads between plants
stories.what: Abu Qir tells the EGX its gas supply is cut by 33% from noon on 8 November, up from 20% since 1 November. It redistributes loads so that two of its three plants run at full capacity and says production continues in line with available gas. MOPCO announced the same cut a day earlier. Abu Qir falls 2.69% and MOPCO 2.59% on Monday.
stories.why: The government saves costly imported gas for power plants.
stories.eg: Lower fertiliser output means fewer export dollars.
stories.egx: Bearish for fertiliser makers until supply is restored.
